title: Property Stolen and Recovered

6.1. Value of Property Stolen
The property worth Rs. 16,241.7 lakhs was stolen in 1981 as compared to stolen property worth Rs. 15,617.2 lakhs in 1980. The value of property stolen from 1976 to 1981 showed an increasing trend except in 1977 when it went down in comparison to 1976. During 1981 it showed an increase of 4.0 per cent over 1980.
6.2. Value of property recovered
The stolen property worth Rs. 5,340.6 lakhs was recovered in 1981 as against Rs. 3,558.6 lakhs in 1980. Table-46 shows that there was a fluctuating trend in the percentage of property recovered to property stolen. The percentage of property recovered to property stolen came down from 35.9 per cent in 1976 to 25.0 per cent in 1977 and again, showed an increasing trend up to 1979 and further came down to 22.8 per cent in 1980 and then went up to 32.9 per cent in 1981.
The statistics on the 'Value of Property Stolen' and percentage of value of property recovered to value of property stolen during 1981 are presented in Table-46 along with similar statistics for the years 1976 to 1980. The statistics relating to value of property stolen and recovered along with the percentage of value of property recovered to value of property stolen during 1981 by States, Union Territories and Metropolitan cities are presented in Table-47.
It is seen that the percentage of value of property recovered to value of property stolen was only 32.9 in the country during 1981 and for the States and Union Territories it was 28.3 and 67.9 respectively while it was 51.2 for the Metropolitan cities taken together.

Among the Metropolitan cities the highest percentage of recovery of the stolen property was recorded in Delhi (70.0) followed by Jaipur (69.9) and Madras (62.0).
6.3. Property stolen and recovered by category of offences
The statistics relating to property stolen and recovered in different categories of offences revealed that the greatest loss of property was recorded under the crime head 'Thefts' and property worth Rs. 8,597.80 lakhs was stolen in 3,97,223 theft cases followed by 'Burglary' (Rs. 3,055.40 lakhs in 1,45,245 cases), 'Robbery' (Rs. 1,813.84 lakhs in 20,729 cases), 'C.B.T.' (Rs. 1,462.25 lakhs in 16,973 cases) and 'Dacoity' (Rs. 1,001.02 lakhs in 11,630 cases). The percentage of property recovered to property stolen was the highest in respect of Robbery cases (67.7 percent), followed by 'Thefts' (32.4 per cent), 'Dacoity' (21.7 per cent) and 'Burglary' (21.7 per cent). It was the minimum for 'Criminal Breach of Trust' (16.6 per cent). The percentage of property recovered to property stolen was highest in respect of 'Cattle' (52.7 per cent) followed by 'Motor Vehicles and Accessories' (49.7 per cent), 'Fire Arms' (43.0 per cent), 'Cycles' (22.9 per cent), 'Wire' (22.0 per cent), and the lowest in respect of 'Explosives' (6.2 per cent). Relevant statistics are presented in Table-48. The number of cases in which property was stolen, the value of property stolen and recovered and percentage of property recovered to value of property stolen according to nature of property has been presented in Table-49.
